lenses.mandate: Judge whether the changed code does what the acceptance criteria require on every path it can be reached through, including error and boundary paths. A finding names the input or path and the wrong outcome it produces there.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria describing the behaviour of the changed code paths

lenses.mandate: Judge whether this change can be made to act against the interests of the system that runs it, and say how an attacker gets there. A hardening suggestion with no attack path is not a finding.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria describing trust boundaries, inputs, and permissions

lenses.mandate: Judge whether the tests shipped with this change would fail if the required behaviour were broken — including the negative, edge, and resiliency cases the criteria enumerate — and whether each test is of the appropriate kind for what it pins. A finding names the failure the missing or inadequate test would have let through; a test that could be added but pins no enumerated behaviour is not a finding.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria that a test is expected to pin, including enumerated failure modes

lenses.mandate: Judge whether the changed code is more complicated, or more costly to run, than the acceptance criteria require. A finding names the requirement the extra structure or cost serves no part of; a stylistic preference is not a finding.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria bounding the scope and cost of the change

lenses.mandate: Judge whether the change's comments and documentation are right-sized: nothing over-documented, no identifiers a reader has no context for, and no narrated history that belongs in the commit log. A refuted alternative stated in the present tense — the plausible wrong design and what breaks under it — is current rationale and stays, so a finding names the episode, not the reason. This lens owns embedded-prose rot — narration, drift, history stated as episode. A finding names the misreading the comment causes; a contradiction with current behaviour or a current decision qualifies without an observed victim. A merely brief comment is not a finding.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria describing what the change must explain and to whom

lenses.mandate: Judge whether the declared interfaces are the right decisions: each signature, data shape, and contract judged as the commitment it pins — what it hides, what it exposes, what every implementation must honor. A finding names the declaration and the obligation it wrongly commits or fails to pin; a preference among equally sound shapes is not a finding.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria describing the decisions the interfaces must pin

lenses.mandate: Judge whether the artifact stays specification: signatures, data shapes, and deliberately failing tests, never implementation. A body, hardening, or optimization in the artifact promotes a consequence into a decision before the evidence for it exists. A finding names the code that exceeds the contract and the premature decision it embeds; a stub returning a constant to satisfy a type checker is not a finding.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria bounding the artifact to declared contracts

lenses.mandate: Judge whether the artifact's deliberately failing tests pin the decisions the criteria enumerate — each enumerated behaviour has a red test that turns green only when the behaviour is honored. A finding names the enumerated decision no failing test pins; a test that could be added but pins no enumerated decision is not a finding.
lenses.acs_hint: the criteria whose decisions the failing tests must pin

lenses.mandate: Judge whether the document contradicts itself, and whether every statement it makes could be settled by an observation. Read the whole document: a change in one section can break a claim in another. A finding names the two statements that conflict, or the one statement no observation could settle.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria the document's own rules and definitions must satisfy

lenses.mandate: Judge whether each acceptance criterion can be converted into one or more tests that fail before the work and pass after it. Name the failing test that is impossible to write.
lenses.acs_hint: the criteria themselves, judged as testable claims

lenses.mandate: Judge whether the document's declared scope and its content agree in both directions: nothing implied but never specified, nothing specified that the scope excludes. A finding names the implied-but-unspecified obligation, or the specified item the declared scope excludes.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria describing what the document must and must not cover

lenses.mandate: Judge whether the proposed design holds together on its own terms and sits coherently in the architecture of the project and module around it. Read the surrounding structure, not only the document. A finding names the structure in the surrounding system that the design contradicts or duplicates.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria describing the design's obligations to the surrounding system

lenses.mandate: Judge whether a competent reader outside this effort could act on the text without asking a question, and whether it says so in as few words as the content allows. A finding names the question an outside reader cannot answer from the text, or the passage whose words outnumber their content; a rewording that answers no such question is not a finding.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria describing how the text must read to an outside reader

lenses.mandate: Judge whether the document contradicts itself: claims restated differently in two places, a term carrying two meanings, rules whose outcomes conflict. A finding names the two places that conflict.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria the document's own claims must satisfy

lenses.mandate: Judge whether the document fits the bigger picture: read the surrounding project material and report where the text contradicts, duplicates, or silently diverges from it. A finding names the surrounding material contradicted, duplicated, or silently diverged from.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria describing the document's obligations to its surroundings

lenses.mandate: Judge whether the text is usable on its own where it is deployed. References to other documents are fine, and an explainer or key section legitimises the identifiers it defines; undefined jargon and cross-references that resolve to nothing are not. Narrated history fails the same test: the reader cannot resolve an episode they were not present for, so it belongs in the commit log. A refuted alternative the document states in the present tense — the plausible wrong design and what breaks under it — is current rationale and stays, so a finding names the episode, not the reason. A finding names the identifier, reference, or episode the deployed reader cannot resolve.
lenses.acs_hint: criteria describing what the deployed text must convey on its own
